QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_10

question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which of the following best describes the MANDATORY requirement for external members of the Investment Committee of an AIF at the time of processing the AIF registration application and launch of schemes?

answer.text: External members must be residents of the GIFT-IFSC zone only.
External members must be former SEBI officials.
External members must be NRI investors who invested in the fund.
External members must be resident Indian citizens. If they are non-resident Indian citizens, the application is processed only after clarifications from the Government and RBI.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/IMD/DF6/CIR/P/2020/209 dated October 22, 2020, external members of the proposed IC must be resident Indian citizens; if non-resident, the application is processed only after clarifications from the Government and RBI. The Trap: There is no GIFT-IFSC restriction, no ex-SEBI-official rule, and no NRI-investor linkage for external IC membership. Cross-Exam Context: Same rule in XIX-C (All-Cat) and XIX-D (Cat I/II). Distinguish from XIX-B distributor exam which does not go this deep. Manager's Pro-Tip: When hiring an external IC member for a Cat III fund, verify residency status under Income-Tax Act (182-day test) at each financial-year start, because a member who later becomes non-resident (say, relocating abroad) can disrupt IC composition mid-year.
